plan: This is a second-price (Vickrey) auction. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding my true value of $35 maximizes my expected profit without risk of overpaying. Bidding lower only reduces my chance of winning without improving my payment terms, and bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high. I'll bid exactly $35.

Truthful bidding is optimal here.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid below my value—doing so only risks losing auctions I could have profitably won, while bidding above value risks losses. With my value at $48, I'll bid exactly $48 to maximize expected profit.
